items.title: 52035_Eddie Durham oral history interview
items.q: He'd get up, finish it, Alan, finish it, Alan.

ctx.x: Because he'd say, Basie, play this for me. Man, I can't read that. Oh, and he'd say, you're going to bring up something now, you're supposed to be an arranger. Sometimes Basie used to help him with the arranging. I'd say, Basie, set down and make up something, because he'd make up a little something, I'd write it down. I'd say, man, you've got terrific ideas, but he wouldn't stick with it. He'd get up, finish it, Alan, finish it, Alan. And that's all he'd want to do. He'd say, now, I'll take this one, Benny. And…
Benny Morton himself, how good a reader was he?
